subject: Greenleaf Health — Multi‑app Governance & Renewal Plan
messages:
From: Jared Lowe <jared.lowe@greenleaf.health>
To: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Cc: Elena Park <epark@greenleaf.health>
Date: 2026-12-20 09:12 -0800
Subject: Expanding to 6 additional apps — governance & renewal questions

Hi Laura,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the pilot has been solid. We are planning to onboard 6 additional internal apps across Marketing, Ops, and Care Insights in Q1 and wanted to align on a few items before we proceed: 

- Key provisioning: can we get separate API keys per app/team or should we use a single token with internal routing?
- Billing & term impact: how does adding these apps affect our current committed capacity and renewal? We are near our committed threshold for Dedicated capacity.
- Governance: any recommended quota/usage guardrails and audit log cadence for sensitive workloads (PHI-touching services)?
- Timeline: we are targeting staged activation starting 2027-01-10.

If you can put together a short mutual action plan (MAP) that covers keys, timeline, and any contract amendment necessary, we can route internally and fast-track.

Appreciate it — Jared

--
Jared Lowe
Director, Platform Integrations
Greenleaf Health
From: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Jared Lowe <jared.lowe@greenleaf.health>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, stephanie_nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-12-20 11:08 -0800
Subject: Re: Expanding to 6 additional apps — governance & renewal questions

Hi Jared — good to hear the pilot went well. I put together a short MAP and attached a draft SOW that shows options for per-app keys vs. tenant-scoped tokens. High level: 

1) Keys and provisioning
   - We can provision per-app keys (recommended) and map each to its own quota and audit stream. This gives the cleanest billing and security posture.
   - Alternative: a single token with project-level routing; lower operational overhead but more complicated RBAC.

2) Billing & term
   - Because you are near your Dedicated commit, the safe path is to amend the existing commitment to add a 20% buffer for Q1 usage with a pro‑rated charge for the remainder of the term, then fold the new baseline into the renewal.
   - If you prefer a pure-usage top-up instead, we can enable burst capacity but that will be billed at on-demand rates.

3) Governance and audit
   - Recommend per-app logging to a central S3/GCS bucket we can ship audit exports to daily.
   - For PHI-touching services, enable event-level tracing and 30‑day retention by default; we can extend retention on request.

4) Timeline and rollout
   - Week 1 (2027-01-10): Provision keys for apps 1–3, enable quotas and audit pipeline.
   - Week 3: Provision apps 4–6, run load smoke tests, enable UX owners.

Attaching a MAP and a light SOW draft for your procurement team. Rafael (cc'd) will outline the exact amendment language for the Dedicated commitment. Can we schedule a 30 minute sync early next week to lock the approach?

Thanks,
Laura

--
Laura Bennett
Head of Account Sales, Enterprise
Redwood Inference
From: rafael_mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.ai>
To: Jared Lowe <jared.lowe@greenleaf.health>, laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, stephanie_nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-12-21 08:34 -0800
Subject: Re: Expanding to 6 additional apps — governance & renewal questions

Jared — following up with the procurement angle and a suggested amendment sketch. Key points: 

- Amendment approach: add a Q1 buffer equal to 20% of current committed vCPU/token throughput. We will pro-rate the buffer for 6 weeks (remainder of current billing period) and then increase the committed baseline for the remainder of the 12‑month term.
- Discount: for committed expansion we can offer a 7% uplift discount on the added baseline (we normally do 10% for multi-year).
- SLA: current SLA stays the same. For guaranteed per-app latency SLOs we can include per-route agreements with an additional SLO fee.

I attached the draft amendment language (SOW-draft-Greenleaf.docx) and a short MAP (GLF-MutualActionPlan-v2.pdf) with owners and dates. Please review and let me know if your procurement team needs net‑30 vs. net‑45.

If you're okay with the amendment sketch Rafael proposes, I can kick off an internal billing estimate and get a formal quote out by EOD Thursday.

-Rafael

Thanks everyone — this is helpful. A few quick answers/asks from our side: 

- Procurement prefers the amendment approach and would like the pro‑rated buffer; net‑30 payment terms are fine.
- For keys we'll take per-app API keys, please include example naming & rotation cadence in the MAP (Elena to own rotation).
- Can you confirm daily audit export format (we need JSONL events with event_type, actor, model, token_count)?
- We'd like the formal quote and an updated MAP by Thursday EOD so our legal/procurement can review before the 2026‑12‑31 budget close.

If you can get the quote and the two-line example audit record attached to the MAP, we can finalize quickly.

Best,
Jared
